- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or weak sentiment-driven corrections.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days — especially after sharp spikes or drops; adjust for recent momentum.
- Overshoots after price spikes — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, leading to overcorrection in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects from recent highs or lows, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early part of forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising — adjust downward for early period.
- When sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, model overreacts — suppress early forecast increases if sentiment is not strongly confirming price momentum.
